Total Amount Paid = ₹4,000 + ₹4,350 = ₹8,350

Total Interest = Total Paid − Principal = 8,350 − 7,000 = ₹1,350

Total Product (Principal × Time) = (7,000 × 3) + (3,000 × 2) = 21,000 + 6,000 = 27,000

Rate (R) = (Total Interest × 100) ÷ Total Product

R = (1,350 × 100) ÷ 27,000 = 5%

**∴ The correct option is C.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Principal (P₁) = ₹7,000

Repayment after 3 years = ₹4,000

New Principal for next 2 years (P₂) = 7,000 − 4,000 = ₹3,000

Total Time = 5 years (3 years + 2 years)

Final Settlement Payment = ₹4,350

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
•

 P = ₹7,000

 Repay ₹4,000

questions.question: Article 123 of the Constitution of India gives the power of enacting Ordinances to who among the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **President's** ability to enact laws is covered in **Article** **123**.
 
• This **authority** is one of the numerous **legislative** ones that the president has.
 
• He may only enact the **ordinance** in the following situations:
 
 
• When neither of the **houses** or both, are in **session**.
 
• There are instances where the President decides it is important to **take** **action** before the **houses** have **gathered**.
 
• An ordinance may be made with a **retroactive** **effect**.
 
• An ordinance passed when both houses are in session is **inherently** **invalid**.
 
• The ordinance must be **approved** by the **Parliament** within **six** **weeks** after its **reconstitution**.
 
• Before the **ordinance** **expires**, actions taken and accomplished under it remain completely in effect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Only when the **Indian parliament** is **not in session** may the **President** of India promulgate an ordinance as a law.
 
• On the **union** **cabinet's** **advice**, the president issues an ordinance.
 
• Similar to this, in Indian states with **unicameral** **legislatures**, the governor can only start an ordinance when the legislative assembly is not in session, and in states with **bicameral** **legislatures** when both the **legislative** **assembly** and the **legislative** **council** are not in session.

questions.question: What is the term used for pricing strategy in which a firm charges different customers difference prices for the same product?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Price discrimination.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• **Price discrimination **is a marketing tactic where customers are charged differently for the **same** **good**** **or **service **depending on what the **vendor **believes they can persuade them to accept.
 
• When a company engages in pure** price discrimination,** they charge the most expensive amount that any given customer will pay.
 
• In more typical forms of price discrimination, the provider divides customers into groups based on particular characteristics and assigns a **different price to each group.**
 
• When a **vendor discriminates **on **price**, every **consumer pays **a **different price **for the **same commodity **or **service**.
 
• The **corporation violates first**-**degree discrimination **by obtaining the highest price for each consumed unit.
 
• **Discounts **on **goods **or **services **when purchased in **quantity **are seen as **second-degree discrimination,** whereas **charging different rates **to certain **customer **groups is regarded as** third-degree discrimination.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Two Part Pricing:**

 
 
• **​**In **two-part pricing, **which is also known as the** two-part tariff,** customers are charged both an admission fee (set price) and a usage cost (per-unit price).
 
• A **phone contract **with a fixed monthly fee and a** minute-by-minute** use fee is an **illustration **of two-part pricing.
 
 
 
• **Price mechanism:**
 
 
• **​**A **price mechanism **in economics is the way that **profits **from **goods **or **services **influence supply and demand, primarily through the price elasticity of demand.
 
• A price mechanism has an impact on** price-haggling **buyers and sellers.
 
 
 
• **Price elasticity:**
 
 
• **​**The relationship between **percentage change **in product's **quantity **demanded and the percentage change in price is known as price elasticity of demand.
 
• It helps economists **comprehend **how **supply **and **demand shift **in response to the changes in **product's price.**

questions.question: In Economics, which of the following curves is 'inverse U-shaped?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marginal product curve.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• A **cost curve **in economics is a **graph** that shows the production costs as a **function** of the **overall** **quantity** **produced**.
 
• **Long-run average cost curves **(LRAC) and **short-run average total cost curves **(SRAC) are both generally expressed as **V-shaped curves.**
 
• However, not all of the curves' shapes may be attributed to the **same causes.**
 
• Because an** increase in output **raises the returns and lowers the overall cost, the Marginal product curve is** inverse-U-shap**ed.
 
• The output and returns are at their peak as the curve continues to **slope** **lower **and approach the phase of **constant returns. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• 
 The slope of the total product curve, which represents the production function plotted against **labour** usage for a certain amount of **capital input usage,** is the** marginal product **of labour.
 
 
• 
 The marginal output of labour is equal to the real pay according to the **neoclassical** **theory** of **competitive markets.**
 
 
• 
 The marginal product of capital is equivalent to its rate of return in aggregate models of **perfect** **competition** when a single good is produced and used for both **consumption** and** capital purposes.**

questions.question: In March 2022, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) increased the eligibility criteria for microfinance loans to a household having an annual income of up to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹3 lakhs.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** removed the interest rate ceiling on the loans and raised the qualifying requirements for **microfinance loans **to **households **with annual incomes of up to** Rs 3 lakh.**
 
• Additionally, it requested that all lenders implement a **board-approved pricing strategy.**
 
• The RBI stated that it will examine the **rates offered **by the **lenders **to ensure that they do not charge** usurious rates.**
 
• The RBI also requested that the** lenders set a cap **on the **cost **of **loans **and associated expenses.
 
• The **microfinance institutions **are expected to provide a prospective borrower with a **standardised simplified **fact sheet that includes** pricing-related information. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• A banking service called **microfinance **provides **unemployed **or** low-income individuals **or **groups **with access to **financial services **that they would not otherwise have.
 
• Through microfinance, people can get **respectable small business loans **in a safe manner that abides by moral lending norms.
 
• The majority of microfinance transactions occur in developing nations including **Uganda**, **Indonesia**, **Serbia**, and **Honduras**.
 
• Like regular **lenders**, **microlenders **impose specific repayment schedules and apply interest to loans.
 
• The **World Bank **estimates that over **500 million **people have benefited from **microfinance-related ventures.**
